video_title: NBA Injuries Shake Up the West | Should OKC Trade Jalen Williams?

quotes.speaker: Wosny Lambre
quotes.summary_phrase: OKC's roster depth and the trade dilemma regarding Jalen Williams
quotes.excerpt: I think they have to make a trade. I think there's no way around this.

text_blocks.speaker: Wosny Lambre
text_blocks.text: I want to talk about what's happening at the top of the West, which is OKC losing Jalen Williams for what we can safely assume is the whole season. That gnarly ankle and leg injury, as well as Chet Holmgren, who tore his labrum. They're saying that's a four to six-month injury, which would mean at best he could come back in the playoffs.

text_blocks.speaker: Jovan Buha
text_blocks.text: We were discussing this in the group chat, and I think they have to make a trade. I think there's no way around this. Looking at their cap situation over the next few years, it probably was going to get to a point where they had to pick between keeping one of Chet or Jalen Williams versus the supporting cast.

quotes.speaker: Wosny Lambre
quotes.summary_phrase: De'Aaron Fox's commitment to the Sacramento Kings organization
quotes.excerpt: De'Aaron Fox, when he was up to be traded, he made the Spurs a destination.
quotes.quote: In the NBA, if you take yourself seriously as an organization, I think you have to be taking this people stuff seriously. And De'Aaron Fox, when he was up to be traded, he made the Spurs a destination, which is a thing that never happens. Nobody ever chooses these people. He chose you guys. You guys are very particular about the kind of characters that you bring in, and he fits the bill of the character of the quintessential San Antonio Spur.

quotes.speaker: Jovan Buha
quotes.summary_phrase: Gordon Hayward's performance and the sunk cost of his injury
quotes.excerpt: I think the fear here is that this is just a sunk asset.
quotes.quote: If we compare to Gordon Hayward, he was first game of the season. He misses the entire rest of the season. And then if you go look at his numbers that first year back, he was a shell of himself. He did bounce back, but he never was as good as Jalen Williams. I think the fear here is that this is just a sunk asset. And what if Jalen Williams is just never the same player again?

quotes.speaker: Wosny Lambre
quotes.summary_phrase: The potential trade of Paolo Banchero and Orlando's roster strategy
quotes.excerpt: Straight up for Paolo Banchero. Works financially.
quotes.quote: I have like 20, but I'll give you three. Straight up for Paolo Banchero. Works financially. Why does Orlando want to do this? They just get a bunch of picks. They can make a more front-centric team, make it less confusing.

quotes.speaker: Jovan Buha
quotes.summary_phrase: Potential trade of Jalen Williams and Jaren Jackson Jr. to New Orleans
quotes.excerpt: What about Jalen Williams and Jaren Jackson Jr. for Lauri Markkanen?
quotes.quote: What about Jalen Williams and Jaren Jackson Jr. for Lauri Markkanen? Let's say Jaren Jackson Jr. is out six to eight weeks. Utah is a little shaky right now. Markkanen himself is dealing with something. If things go south with Utah and they're not even looking like a play-in team potentially, do they flip Markkanen for Jalen Williams?

quotes.speaker: Wosny Lambre
quotes.summary_phrase: The impact of team culture and employee management on player movement
quotes.excerpt: You're actually incentivized to do as little as possible while you're there.
quotes.quote: You show up to work and you work an hourly position at your job, you're not incentivized to work hard. You're not incentivized to do better in your position. You're actually incentivized to do as little as possible while you're there because your pay doesn't change based off of how hard you work. But as a human being with some goddamn sense, you don't want to watch your fellow coworkers take shit seriously and do all of the work for you. You want to take pride in what you do.

quotes.speaker: Jovan Buha
quotes.summary_phrase: The defensive struggles of the Lakers and the need for lineup changes
quotes.excerpt: I think it needs to be a lineup change. I think Quentin Grimes should start over Matisse Thybulle.
quotes.quote: I've been really concerned with the defense to start the season. The caliber of offenses that they've played to be the number 22 defense. I understand they had the most roster turnover in the league. Nine new players, brand new starting group, brand new rotation, all those things. New defensive scheme. It's going to take some time to adjust. But this is not the caliber of opponent you should be a bottom nine defense against. I think it needs to be a lineup change. I think Quentin Grimes should start over Matisse Thybulle. Quentin Grimes is their best point-of-attack defender in my opinion. He's also the best at guarding quicker players.

quotes.speaker: Wosny Lambre
quotes.summary_phrase: The Knicks' performance in the first three quarters of the playoffs
quotes.excerpt: that second and third quarter was the Knicks of the playoffs on display
quotes.quote: The Knicks go down 38 to 25 after the first. So they give up 38 points in the first quarter, then they give up a combined 25 in the second and third quarter. And that second and third quarter was the Knicks of the playoffs on display. Hands and arms everywhere, wreaking havoc, causing turnovers, getting out on the break, nice ball movement on offense. Get that thing ring around the Rosie.

quotes.speaker: Wosny Lambre
quotes.summary_phrase: The Pistons' offense is not ready for the big leagues
quotes.excerpt: I just think their offense is not ready for the big leagues at all
quotes.quote: The Pistons conversely, even in that win against Boston, I just think their offense is not ready for the big leagues at all. You are giving Sart Thompson, I get it, you paid the shit out of him, he has to play. He is a zero on offense. Obviously I get it, Jaylen Duren didn't play. Paul Reed is your second best offensive threat? Really? That can't be a championship formula.

quotes.speaker: Wosny Lambre
quotes.summary_phrase: The Knicks are the team with the least amount of stuff to figure out
quotes.excerpt: I just think they're the team with the least amount of stuff to figure out
quotes.quote: Watching them yesterday, it just reminded me why I don't care what happens this regular season as long as the team is physically intact by the time the playoffs happen. I just think they're the team with the least amount of stuff to figure out come playoff time. Least amount of issues, most continuity. Not just that the team has been together, but they've been through the playoffs, made deep runs together.

quotes.speaker: Wosny Lambre
quotes.summary_phrase: The Knicks are too old to play hard on defense all season
quotes.excerpt: the Knicks are too old to play hard on defense to the degree that they need to
quotes.quote: Last night was just a reminder for me is just like, yo, the Knicks are too old to play hard on defense to the degree that they need to be dominant all season long. But when they do it, they are an elite team in the NBA. There is just no other way to put that.

quotes.speaker: Wosny Lambre
quotes.summary_phrase: The Pistons need to trade for a shot creator
quotes.excerpt: everything that's not nailed down to go get somebody who can help you with that shot creation stuff
quotes.quote: I think y'all should be going all in, everything that's not nailed down to go get somebody who can help you with that shot creation stuff. Kyrie, that's the one that's probably my favorite. We've seen him work next to the big ball handler mold. Cade is probably the closest thing to Luka in terms of his style of play and just being that big ball handler, shot creator. What do you think about a Devin Booker?

quotes.speaker: Danny Green
quotes.summary_phrase: The Pistons need an offensive infusion
quotes.excerpt: they need an offensive infusion here
quotes.quote: Maybe a more realistic one is Tyler Herro, which I'm not as sold on, but Tyler Herro compared to what they currently have, they need that. They need an offensive infusion here. And if they get that, then I think the conversation changes a bit and they do have enough defense toughness. I see the vision, but I also wonder like who are you trading in that case and what does that trade potentially look like?

quotes.speaker: Wosny Lambre
quotes.summary_phrase: The Pistons should not trade Jaden Ivey for a star
quotes.excerpt: is it possible that they'd be giving up in a Sart Thompson and the Devin Booker deal
quotes.quote: Is it possible that they'd be giving up in a Sart Thompson and the Devin Booker deal? You know what I mean? Like, no. But how do you make that money work? It's Cade, it's Cade and a Sart and anything else is tradable. Although if you trade Duren and then you don't get a good center back, now you're starting Paul Reed. Do I love him as a bench big, but not as a starter?

quotes.speaker: Wosny Lambre
quotes.summary_phrase: Ernie Johnson is the heartbeat of the show
quotes.excerpt: Ernie is the straw that stirs the drink
quotes.quote: Ernie is the straw that stirs the drink, and he is the ingredient that makes this an untouchable studio show. I think somebody else with Chuck and Kenny and Shaq, like those personalities are so magnetic and so fun and care free, and Chuck's willingness to say anything, to speak his mind into a microphone in a way that most ex-players just don't, they're just too scared to say something negative about the fraternity, in a way that Chuck just doesn't give a fuck. I think that show would still be good. What takes it to special stratospheric is Ernie.

quotes.speaker: Danny Green
quotes.summary_phrase: Ernie Johnson's impact on the studio show
quotes.excerpt: he's the magic Johnson of being the point guard on these studio shows
quotes.quote: He's the Magic Johnson of being the point guard on these studio shows and like just to your point, he just had this the perfect balance of knowing when to step in with a quip, when to back up and let the guys do their thing and then also keeping it pushing because those guys we know can yapp and they can talk for hours and just keep a topic going and he would find artful ways to step in and redirect the conversation or move it on to the next subject and just his timing and the the chemistry that they had is special. I mean it is the best studio show, certainly the best sports studio show. It might be the best studio show ever.
